topic: am / is / are — the verb 'to be' in the present
focus: I am, you are, he/she/it is, we/they are; contractions I'm, you're, it's; negative 'I'm not', questions 'Are you...?'

topic: my / your / his / her — possessive adjectives, and 'This is...'
focus: my, your, his, her, our, their; 'This is my mother'; 's for possession: Tom's sister

topic: Telling the time and 'at / on / in' for time
focus: What time is it? It's three o'clock, half past seven; at 7, on Monday, in the morning; numbers 1-20 pattern

topic: I like / I don't like — present simple with 'like' and 'want'
focus: I like tea, I don't like coffee, Do you like...? Yes I do / No I don't; I want, I'd like (polite)

topic: There is / There are and in / on / under
focus: There is a table, There are two chairs; Is there...? There isn't; prepositions of place in, on, under, next to

topic: Present simple: I work / she works — the third-person -s
focus: I/you/we/they + verb, he/she/it + verb-s; does/doesn't; go→goes, watch→watches; daily routine

topic: a / an / the, and plural -s
focus: a book, an apple; the when both know which one; plurals -s/-es, irregular child→children; adjectives come before nouns: a red car

topic: I have / she has, and 'I feel + adjective'
focus: have/has, don't have; I feel tired, I'm happy; 'I have a headache' vs Turkish 'başım ağrıyor'

topic: Where is...? and imperatives for directions
focus: Where is the bank? It's near the park; Go straight, turn left, stop, wait; Don't + verb

topic: It's + adjective for weather, and can / can't
focus: It's sunny, it's cold, it's raining; I can swim, I can't drive, Can you...?; no 'to' after can

topic: Irregular plurals and 'How many...?'
focus: sheep/sheep, mouse/mice, child/children, man/men, foot/feet; 'How many cows are there?' with 'There are two'; 'a lot of' vs numbers

topic: Yes/No questions with do/does and short answers
focus: Do you sing? Does she work? — Yes, I do / No, she doesn't; the -s goes to 'does', not the verb; 'What do you do?' for jobs

topic: Past simple: was / were and regular -ed verbs
focus: I was, you were; worked, played, studied; didn't + base verb; Did you...?; -ed pronunciation /t/ /d/ /ɪd/

topic: Past simple: the irregular verbs you actually need
focus: go→went, have→had, see→saw, take→took, come→came, get→got; the 20 most common; no -ed on these

topic: The future: going to and will
focus: going to for plans and evidence, will for decisions now and predictions; won't; I'll help you

topic: Question words: who, what, where, when, why, how
focus: word order Wh + do/does/did + subject + verb; How many / How often / How long; Turkish 'ne, kim, nerede' mapping

topic: Comparatives and superlatives
focus: bigger, more expensive; the biggest, the most expensive; than; good→better→best, bad→worse→worst; as...as

topic: Countable and uncountable: some / any / much / many
focus: How much money? How many shirts?; some in positives, any in questions/negatives; a lot of; a bit of

topic: Present continuous: I'm going, she's waiting
focus: am/is/are + -ing for now and for arranged plans; spelling: run→running, take→taking; stative verbs don't (know, like)

topic: Adverbs of frequency and where they go
focus: always, usually, often, sometimes, never; before the main verb, after 'be'; already / still / yet

topic: too / enough / very / a bit — degree words
focus: too tired to go, not old enough, very happy, a bit shy; -ed vs -ing adjectives: bored / boring

topic: Prepositions of time and place: in / on / at, the full picture
focus: in 2020, in summer, in the morning; on Monday, on 5 May; at 6, at night, at the weekend; in the park, on the beach, at home

topic: like / love / hate + -ing, and 'would like to'
focus: I love singing, she hates waiting; 'would like to + verb' for polite wishes: I'd like to see that film; contrast 'like' (general) vs 'would like' (now)

topic: Invitations and suggestions: Let's, Shall we, Why don't we, How about
focus: Let's + verb, Shall we + verb?, Why don't we + verb?, How about + -ing?; accepting (Sounds good / I'd love to) and refusing politely (I'm afraid I can't)

topic: Present perfect: have / has + past participle; ever / never
focus: I've seen it, She has never been; life experience without a time; been vs gone; contrast with Turkish -miş/-di

topic: Present perfect vs past simple: since, for, already, yet, just
focus: I've lived here for 5 years / since 2019; I lived there in 2010 (finished time); already, yet, just placement

topic: Modal verbs: should, must, have to, might, could
focus: advice vs obligation vs possibility; must vs have to; mustn't vs don't have to (the classic trap); no -s, no 'to'

topic: First conditional: If it rains, we'll stay in
focus: if + present, will; unless; when vs if; zero conditional for facts

topic: The passive: is made, was built, will be sent
focus: be + past participle; when the doer doesn't matter; by + agent; present, past, future forms

topic: Second conditional: If I were you, I'd see a doctor
focus: if + past, would; imaginary present; 'If I were' not 'was' in advice; would/could/might

topic: Relative clauses: who, which, that, where, whose
focus: the app that I downloaded; the friend who called; defining vs non-defining (commas); when you can drop 'that'

topic: Gerunds and infinitives: enjoy doing / want to do
focus: verbs followed by -ing (enjoy, finish, avoid), by to (want, decide, hope); stop doing vs stop to do; after prepositions -ing

topic: used to / would for past habits, and be used to
focus: I used to smoke; didn't use to; be/get used to + -ing (alışkın olmak); would for repeated past actions

topic: Reported speech: he said that..., she told me...
focus: tense backshift (is→was, will→would); say vs tell; reporting questions: asked if / asked where

topic: Quantifiers: a little, a few, plenty of, not much, not many
focus: a little + uncountable (a little salt), a few + countable (a few onions); 'not much / not many'; 'plenty of / lots of' with both; 'How much / How many' — with recipe examples

topic: Question tags: You're coming, aren't you?
focus: positive statement → negative tag and vice versa; auxiliary matching (do/does/did/will/can/be); 'I'm..., aren't I?'; intonation: falling = checking, rising = real question

topic: Linking words: however, whereas, therefore, despite, although
focus: contrast, cause, result; punctuation and position; despite + noun/-ing vs although + clause; in spite of

topic: Narrative tenses: past perfect and past continuous
focus: had done for earlier past; was doing for background; while / when; telling a story in order

topic: Third and mixed conditionals: If they had listened, ...
focus: if + past perfect, would have; regret and hindsight; mixed: If I had studied, I would be a doctor now

topic: Passive in all tenses and 'It is said that...'
focus: has been tested, is being studied, will have been completed; impersonal passive: It is believed that; He is thought to be

topic: Future forms: will / going to / present continuous / future perfect / future continuous
focus: choosing by meaning; by 2030 we will have...; this time next year I'll be working; timetable present simple

topic: Modals of deduction: must have, can't have, might have
focus: present: must be, can't be, might be; past: must have been, can't have done; degrees of certainty

topic: Reported speech, advanced: questions, commands, reporting verbs
focus: asked whether, told him to, suggested doing, denied having; time/place shifts (tomorrow→the next day)

topic: wish / if only / would rather / it's time
focus: I wish I had (present regret), I wish I had gone (past), I wish you would stop; I'd rather you didn't; it's time we left

topic: Articles, advanced: the with generalizations and zero article
focus: The tiger is endangered vs Tigers are...; zero article with abstract/plural; the with rivers, oceans, superlatives; no article with 'nature', 'society'

topic: Participle clauses: Having finished..., Walking home, ...
focus: -ing for simultaneous/cause, having + pp for earlier; past participle for passive; the subject must match (dangling participle trap)

topic: Causatives: have something done, get someone to do, make / let someone do
focus: have/get + object + past participle (have the report checked); get someone to do vs make someone do vs let someone do; 'have someone do' (AmE); passive-like meaning without saying who

topic: Advanced comparison: the more..., the better; twice as... as; by far; nowhere near
focus: 'the + comparative, the + comparative' (the further you go, the cheaper it gets); multipliers 'twice / three times as ... as'; intensifying superlatives 'by far the', 'easily the'; softening 'nowhere near as', 'not quite as'

topic: Inversion for emphasis: Never have I..., Not only... but also
focus: negative adverbials trigger inversion: never, rarely, not only, no sooner, under no circumstances; auxiliary before subject; formal tone

topic: Cleft sentences: What I need is..., It was Tom who...
focus: what-clefts, it-clefts, all-clefts; putting the focus where you want it; the one thing that...

topic: How phrasal verbs work: separable, inseparable, three-part
focus: pick it up vs pick up it; look after her (inseparable); put up with; particle meanings (up = completion, out = disappearance)

topic: Nominalisation: turning verbs into nouns for academic style
focus: implement → the implementation of; analyse → analysis; when it helps (concise, formal) and when it kills a sentence

topic: Register and hedging: arguably, it would seem, to some extent
focus: formal vs informal choices (purchase/buy, in addition/also); hedging verbs and adverbs; avoiding overclaiming in writing

topic: The subjunctive and formal 'were': I suggest that he be..., Were it not for...
focus: that + base verb after suggest/demand/insist; if I were; were it not for, had it not been for (inverted conditionals)

topic: Complex noun phrases and ellipsis
focus: stacked modifiers (a government-backed small-business loan scheme); leaving out repeated words; reduced relative clauses

topic: Cause, effect and concession: owing to, thereby, albeit, notwithstanding
focus: owing to / due to / on account of; thereby + -ing; albeit + phrase; notwithstanding; for all + noun

topic: Fronting and emphasis: Such was..., So + adjective, Little did they know
focus: fronting objects and complements; so/such inversion; emphatic do; rhetorical structures in speeches

topic: Degrees of certainty and stance: may well, could hardly, bound to, is likely to
focus: modal + adverb combinations; be bound to, be liable to, be likely to; hedged judgement vs strong claim; tentative language

topic: Gradable vs ungradable adjectives and their intensifiers
focus: very/extremely/rather + gradable (very moving); absolutely/utterly/completely + ungradable (absolutely sublime, ✗ very sublime); 'quite' meaning 'fairly' vs 'completely'; 'pretty', 'somewhat', 'downright' in register

topic: Advanced conditionals: inverted (Had I known), unless, provided that, but for, otherwise
focus: Inversion in formal conditionals: Had she known..., Were it to fail..., Should you need...; 'unless' = if not; 'provided / providing that', 'on condition that', 'as long as'; 'but for' + noun; 'otherwise' as a conditional link
